name: OpenScrub-Intel
description: Local video redaction with human review — Intel GPU build. Detects and blurs PII in videos and screen recordings — faces, whole people (silhouette body masking), license plates, names, SSNs, emails, addresses, card numbers, and more, plus your own custom regex categories — with OpenVINO-accelerated detection (OCR, faces, plates, person models) and Quick Sync hardware encoding on any Intel iGPU (Gen 9+) or Arc card. Pass /dev/dri through (preconfigured below) to enable the GPU; without it everything still runs on the CPU. The image ships Intel's media driver — no host driver install needed. Everything runs on this server; no footage leaves your network. Best-effort redaction: always review output before sharing.

paths.name: Appdata
paths.description: Jobs (contains the sensitive uploads and reports!), review decisions, certificates, zones, downloaded models, encryption vault. Everything OpenScrub stores lives here — the container itself is disposable.

paths.name: Media
paths.description: Optional read-only mount of your media share so the 'path on the server' picker can process files without uploading them through the browser.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: HTTPS web interface (self-signed certificate — your browser warns once, or install your own cert in App settings).

variables.name: Access token (optional)
variables.description: Leave empty for open access on your LAN, or set a secret to require it on every request (recommended if others use your network). The WebUI URL becomes https://ip:8384/?token=SECRET on first visit.

variables.name: OPENSCRUB_MEDIA_ROOT
variables.description: Confines the server-path picker to this directory tree. Leave set to /media to match the Media mount; clear it to allow any container path.

devices.name: Intel GPU
devices.description: Intel GPU device for Quick Sync encoding and OpenVINO inference. Remove on a server without an Intel GPU — OpenScrub falls back to CPU automatically.
